name: Google Play Data safety section
plain: A Play Store listing section where developers declare data collected, shared, and security practices.
meaning: Required for all apps since 20 July 2022. Developers must count SDK collection too. Google may reject or remove apps whose behavior does not match.

android.store_policy: Required for all apps, including those with no data collected; declare collection, sharing, encryption in transit, deletion request path
android.api_surface: Play Console > App content > Data safety
android.note: Deadline 20 July 2022; user data deletion link required for apps with account creation.

ios.note: Apple's equivalent is the nutrition label.

limits.headline: Can tell you what the app says it collects and shares, on its Play Store page
limits.user_action: You open the app page in Google Play and scroll to Data safety
can: List what data types the developer says it collects or shares
Show if you can ask to delete your data, with a link for apps with accounts
Count data that third party tools collect too
cannot: Prove the developer told the truth; Google may reject or remove apps that do not match
Appear on iPhone; Apple has a nutrition label instead
Change what the app collects, since it is a label only
limits.reach_label: A label on the store page
limits.differs: This is Google Play only, required since 20 July 2022. Apple uses privacy labels.

story.what_it_is: A box on every Play Store page where the developer lists what data the app collects.

marketing.name: Data safety section
marketing.pitch: Developers share what data an app collects, shares and how it protects it.

story.for_you: Before you install, you can see whether the app collects your location, contacts or purchases, and whether it shares that data with others.
story.for_makers: Makers must count what their ad and analytics tools collect too. Google can remove apps whose behavior differs from the form, so teams audit SDKs before each release.

use_cases.example: A social app lists photos, contacts and location as collected and shared with partners.
A puzzle game declares 'device ID' and 'ads data' because its ad network collects them.
A period tracker says that health data is encrypted and can be deleted on request.
A bank app marks account info collected for app function only, not shared.
A researcher compares the label with real traffic and finds apps that under reported data sent to trackers.
Parents scan labels to pick a game that says no data is shared.

story.android_note: Required for all Play apps since 20 July 2022.
story.ios_note: Apple has a similar label, with different categories.

history.change: Data safety required for all apps from 20 July 2022
